# Equilinox ## Where is the options page? This is not a core-supported game, so there is not options page. You can create a yaml file using the Archipelago Options creator. ### `goal_selection`: Currently, there are two possible goal conditions: | Option | Description | | ----------- | ----------- | | `evolve_camel` | Evolve a Camel | | `completionist` | Complete every task | Recommendations for additional goal conditions are welcome. ### `free_evolution`: Default: `true`. If `true`, starting an evolution costs 0 DP. The other requirements must still be met. If `false`, the vanilla behavior remains (charging DP to start an evolution). ### `tasks_reward_dp`: Default: `true`. If `true`, tasks will give their normal DP amount upon completion, in addition to sending a check. If `false`, completing tasks just sends a check, and some of the small filler DP items are replaced with larger DP items. ### `starting_dp`: Default: `5000`. Range: `2500` - `100000`. The vanilla default starting amount is 2,500 DP. The actual starting DP value will be close to the value of this setting, but not exact. ### `itempool_dp`: Default: `150000`. Range: `0` - `500000`. Can be used to add additional large DP items to the item pool. As with `starting_dp`, the actual value of the added DP items will be close to this, but not exact. ### `size_checks`: Default: `true`. Include checks for breeding species of size 1.10 and size 1.20. Adds 288 checks (or 286 if `evolve_camel` is the goal). ## What is the goal condition? See YAML options above for a description of the possible goal conditions. ## What items could appear in other worlds? Currently, there are only two types of items. All of the base species need to be unlocked by an item (eg, "Sheep Permit" to unlock the sheep), and DP can be received in varying amounts (100 - 100,000). Filler DP items range from 100dp to 10,000dp, with amounts around 1,000 most common. Suggestions for additional items / item types are welcome. ## What do location checks look like? Currently, there are two types of checks that are always included:
  • Task Checks - each task sends a check upon completion (60 checks, or 59 if "Completionist" is the goal)
  • Evolution Checks - evolving a species for the first time sends a check (107 checks, or 106 if "Camel" is the goal)
In the yaml, you have the option to turn on additional checks:
  • Size Checks - breeding a species of size 1.10 is a check, and breeding a species of size 1.20 is a check, for each species (288 checks, or 286 if "Camel" is the goal)
Additional optional checks planned but not yet implemented:
  • More trait checks
  • Biome checks
  • Species count checks

# Equilinox Archipelago Setup Guide > [!IMPORTANT] > Currently, the mod only supports the Windows version of the game (and has only been tested on the Steam installation). I hope to add support for other operating systems in the future. ## Host Only the host needs to have the Archipelago Client installed. General archipelago installation / world generation will not be covered here, instead see [the official guide](https://archipelago.gg/tutorial/Archipelago/setup_en). The host needs the `equilinox.apworld` file found in (ADD LINK). Download this file, then double-click it to automatically place it in the `custom_worlds` folder. ## Player You need to own a copy of the game to run this mod, it is not a stand-alone application. Download the latest `EquilinoxAP.zip` file from (ADD LINK). Opening this zip file should show a similarly named folder; place this `EquilinoxAP` folder into the installation directory of the game. If you installed the game via Steam, you can find this by going to `Manage -> Browse local files` from the game's library page. After doing this, the game directory should look something like this: > [!WARNING] > The mod should not be able to touch your existing save files, since it will create a new folder for AP saves. However, to be safe, I recommend backing up your existing save files. To do this, create a copy of the `Equilinox_0_Saves` folder somewhere safe. On a fresh installation of the mod, this `EquilinoxAP` folder should have three files (the mod .jar and two .bat files): To run the game with the Archipelago mod, double click the `Run Equilinox AP.bat` file. A terminal window will open, but you can close this if you'd like. > [!CAUTION] > The console window logs information about the game (saved in the `APEqLog.log` file), including the AP Server connection info (the host, slot, *and password*) in plain text. You should close this window if you are streaming the game anywhere, just to be safe. When running the game this way, a new UserConfigs file is created with the default settings; if you would like to copy use the same options as the vanilla game (graphic settings, etc), copy the `Equilinox_0_UserConfigs.dat` file from the root directory into the EquilinoxAP folder. To run the game without the Archipelago mod, open the game via Steam or the original .exe file -- the mod is run if and only if one of the .bat files in the EquilinoxAP folder is used to start the game. # Connecting to a multiworld ## For the first time After running the game via the mod loader, the main menu should look like this (notice the mod version number under the title, and the word "Archipelago" on the New World button):
To connect to a multiworld for the first time, click the `New World (Archipelago)` button and input the connection information:
> [!IMPORTANT] > To edit a text field, click the square button on the right-hand side of it. Then click that button again to stop editing that field before you start editing the next field, > or you will be typing in both fields at the same time (see Known Issues). Then select the desired world options (note, only "Normal" mode is supported, so the option to change the Game Mode has been removed) and click `Generate World & Connect`. You can make the World Name whatever you want\* -- it does not have to start with "\[AP\]". \**Be weary of including special characters (see the Known Issues section)* ## Reconnecting to an existing world To reload an existing world, simply load the save file for the world and the mod will automatically attempt to reconnect (the slot, host, and password are saved in the save file): Notice that the save preview does not display the AP connection info for that save yet. This is something I plan to add eventually, but in the meantime, if you are playing in more than one multiworld at once, it may be best to set the world names accordingly when creating them. ## Changing connection info If the server port changes, or if you made a typo when creating the save file and don't want to back out an make a new world, you can change this in-game by clicking the "Archipelago Settings" button on the toolbar: > [!CAUTION] > The menu that opens when you click this button will display the server password in plain text, as does the new world generation menu. I plan to address this in a future update. You can then update the connection info and click "Connect". Eventually, I plan on adding info about completion progress and connection status to this menu. # Updating the Mod To update the mod, you can replace the entire `EquilinoxAP` folder with the new one from the new .zip file. This will reset your config file, so copying that (the `Equilinox_0_UserConfigs.dat` file in the EquilinoxAP folder) first may be desirable. Replacing the EquilinoxAP folder will *not* touch your existing save files, since they are saved in the `Equilinox_AP_Saves` folder in the game directory. However, you should still pay attention to compatibility warnings in the release notes for a new version.

# Equilinox AP Archipelago client for the game *Equilinox*.
Table of Contents
  1. Setup Instructions
  2. Connecting to a Multiworld
  3. Updating the Mod
  4. YAML Options
  5. Checks/Items
  6. Known Issues
  7. Reporting Issues
# Download the Latest Release [Here](https://github.com/AAces17/EquilinoxAPClient/releases/latest) > [!IMPORTANT] > Currently, the mod only supports the Windows version of the game (and has only been tested on the Steam installation). I hope to add support for other operating systems in the future. ## Setup Instructions ### Host Only the host needs to have the Archipelago Client installed. General archipelago installation / world generation will not be covered here, instead see [the official guide](https://archipelago.gg/tutorial/Archipelago/setup_en). The host needs the `equilinox.apworld` file found in the [Releases](https://github.com/AAces17/EquilinoxAPClient/releases/latest) tab. Download this file, then double-click it to automatically place it in the `custom_worlds` folder. [Click here to view the source code of the .apworld file](https://github.com/AAces17/AAcesArchipelago/tree/main/worlds/equilinox). ### Player You need to own a copy of the game to run this mod, it is not a stand-alone application. Download the latest `EquilinoxAP.zip` file from the [Releases](https://github.com/AAces17/EquilinoxAPClient/releases/latest) tab. Opening this zip file should show a similarly named folder; place this `EquilinoxAP` folder into the installation directory of the game. If you installed the game via Steam, you can find this by going to `Manage -> Browse local files` from the game's library page. After doing this, the game directory should look something like this: > [!WARNING] > The mod should not be able to touch your existing save files, since it will create a new folder for AP saves. However, to be safe, I recommend backing up your existing save files. To do this, create a copy of the `Equilinox_0_Saves` folder somewhere safe. On a fresh installation of the mod, this `EquilinoxAP` folder should have a `res` folder and three files (the mod .jar and two .bat files): To run the game with the Archipelago mod, double click the `Run Equilinox AP.bat` file. A terminal window will open, but you can close this if you'd like. When running the game this way, a new UserConfigs file is created with the default settings; if you would like any options you changed (graphic settings, etc) to carry over to the modded launch, copy the `Equilinox_0_UserConfigs.dat` file from the root directory into the EquilinoxAP folder. Alternatively, just change the settings again once the game loads, after which they will be saved. To run the game without the Archipelago mod, open the game via Steam or the original .exe file -- the mod is run if and only if one of the .bat files in the EquilinoxAP folder is used to start the game. ## Connecting to a multiworld ### For the first time After running the game via the mod loader, the main menu should look something like this. If you see a rainbow oval instead of the logo, that means the mod failed to load the images.
To connect to a multiworld for the first time, click the `New World (Archipelago)` button and input the connection information. To edit a text field, click the square button on the right-hand side of it. Then click that button again to stop editing that field before you start editing the next field, or you will be typing in both fields at the same time (see Known Issues).
Then select the desired world options (note, only "Normal" mode is supported, so the option to change the Game Mode has been removed) and click `Generate World & Connect`. You can make the World Name whatever you want\* -- it does not have to start with "\[AP\]". > [!IMPORTANT] > Whenever you launch the game via the mod loader, you *must* either create a new world with the `New World` button, or load an existing world with the `Load World` button. Pressing the `Play` button without first > doing one of these will open up a default world, where nothing is saved and you can not connect to a multiworld. If you accidentally press `Play`, just press esc to return to the main menu and connect properly. > > Once connected, you *can* use the `Play` button to return to the game from the menu. \**Be weary of including special characters in the name of a save file (see the Known Issues section)* ### Reconnecting to an existing world To reload an existing world, simply load the save file for the world and the mod will automatically attempt to reconnect (the connection info is saved in the save file): Notice that the save preview does not display the AP connection info for that save yet. This is something I plan to add eventually, but in the meantime, if you are playing in more than one multiworld at once, it may be best to set the world names accordingly when creating them. ### Changing connection info If the server port changes, or if you made a typo when creating the save file and don't want to back out an make a new world, you can change this in-game by clicking the "Archipelago Settings" button on the toolbar: > [!CAUTION] > The menu that opens when you click this button will display the server password in plain text, as does the new world generation menu. I plan to address this in a future update. You can then update the connection info and click "Connect". You can also view the connection status and goal progress in this menu. Note that this information does not update in real-time; you need to close and open the menu again to refresh it. ## Updating the Mod To update the mod, you can replace the entire `EquilinoxAP` folder with the new one from the new .zip file. This will reset your config file, so copying that (the `Equilinox_0_UserConfigs.dat` file in the EquilinoxAP folder) first may be desirable. Replacing the EquilinoxAP folder will *not* touch your existing save files, since they are saved in the `Equilinox_AP_Saves` folder in the game directory. However, you should still pay attention to compatibility warnings in the release notes for a new version. ## YAML Options ### `goal_selection`: Currently, there are two possible goal conditions: | Option | Description | | ----------- | ----------- | | `evolve_species` | Evolve a set number of species from a list | | `completionist` | Complete every task (default) | Recommendations for additional goal conditions are welcome. ### `evo_goal_species`: Default: `['Camel', 'Giant Cactus']`. Does nothing if Goal Condition is not 'Evolve Species' (`evolve_species`). The set of species from which you will need to evolve X to goal, where X is given by 'Evolution Goal Count' (`evo_goal_count`). ### `evo_goal_count`: Default: `0`. Range: `0` - `107`. Does nothing if Goal Condition is not 'Evolve Species' (`evolve_species`). Sets how many of the species selected in 'Evolution Goal Species Requirements' (`evo_goal_species`) you need to evolve to complete the goal. Setting this to 0 or to a number greater than the number of selected species means you will need to evolve *all* of the selected species to complete the goal. ### `free_evolution`: Default: `true`. If `true`, starting an evolution costs 0 DP. The other requirements must still be met. If `false`, the vanilla behavior remains (charging DP to start an evolution). ### `tasks_reward_dp`: Default: `true`. If `true`, tasks will give their normal DP amount upon completion, in addition to sending a check. If `false`, completing tasks just sends a check, and some of the small filler DP items are replaced with larger DP items. ### `starting_dp`: Default: `5000`. Range: `2500` - `500000`. The vanilla default starting amount is 2,500 DP. The actual starting DP value will be close to the value of this setting, but not exact. ### `itempool_dp`: Default: `200000`. Range: `0` - `1000000`. Can be used to add additional large DP items to the item pool. As with `starting_dp`, the actual value of the added DP items will be close to this, but not exact. ### `dp_per_min_bonus_count`: Default: `10`. Range: `0` - `40`. Adds this many 'Progressive DP/Min Bonus' items to the pool. Each one of these received gives an increasing amount of additional dp/min (see the Items Section below for more information). If set to 0, at least one animal permit will almost certainly be in an early sphere (though this is still likely even if this option is nonzero). ### `size_checks`: Default: `true`. Include checks for breeding species of size 1.10 and size 1.20. Adds 288 checks. ## Goal / Check / Item Information ### Goal options See YAML options above for a description of the possible goal conditions. ### Checks Currently, there are two types of checks that are always included:
  • Task Checks - each task sends a check upon completion (60 checks, or 59 if "Completionist" is the goal)
  • Evolution Checks - evolving a species for the first time sends a check (107 checks)
In the yaml, you have the option to turn on additional checks:
  • Size Checks - breeding a species of size 1.10 is a check, and breeding a species of size 1.20 is a check, for each species (288 checks)
Additional optional checks planned but not yet implemented:
  • More trait checks
  • Biome checks
  • Species count checks
### Items Currently, there are only three types of items:
  • All of the base species need to be unlocked by an item (eg, "Sheep Permit" to unlock the sheep)
  • DP can be received in varying amounts (100 - 250,000)
  • If enabled in the YAML, up to 40 "Progressive DP/Min Bonus" items can be added to the item pool. Each of these received grants a permanent boost to your dp/min according to following formula: if you've received 'n' of these, you will have a bonus of 15(n2+n) dp/min.
For example: | \# "Progressive DP/Min Bonus" items received | Total bonus to dp/min | | ----------- | ----------- | | 0 | 0 | | 1 | 30 | | 2 | 90 | | 3 | 180 | | 5 | 450 | | 10 | 1650 | | 20 | 6300 | | 30 | 13950 | | 40 | 24600 | Filler DP items range from 100dp to 25,000dp, with amounts around 5,000 most common. Suggestions for additional items / item types are welcome. ## Known Issues
  • On pages with multiple text input fields, you click the icon that looks like a pen in a square to edit the field. You then need to click it again to stop editing that field before editing the next text field. This happens because I am using the game's built-in text field object, which does not automatically deselect when you select a different one (because in the vanilla game, there are never 2+ text fields in the same menu). This is something I'd like to fix because it is kind of annoying, but it doesn't break anything. Since it will likely be somewhat involved to actually fix, it'll be left as-is for now.
  • Certain characters in a world (save file) name stop the game from loading the world properly. I know of "-" and "." breaking things, so if you put these in the "World Name" field, it just removes them before creating the world. If you create a world that later will not show up in the "load world" menu, send me the world save file and I'll take a look at it (see below for instructions on how to do this, in the Reporting Issues section).
  • If the mod fails to load the images, they are replaced with a rainbow wheel. This is most noticable on the main menu, where the game logo would get replaced with a rainbow oval. This is not an issue in and of itself, but it does mean there was an issue loading the assets. Make sure there is a folder called "res" in the mod folder, and that it contains .png files.
  • Deathlink is not currently supported. If you have ideas for what deathlink would look like in this game, feel free to share in the Equilinox thread in the AP discord server.
## Reporting Issues Feel free to report bugs or other issues in the Equilinox thread on the AP discord server, or in the "Issues" tab on this Github repository. If you encounter a bug, please make a copy of the `APEqLog.log` file in the EquilinoxAP mod directory before restarting the game (this file gets wiped each time the game starts). If the game *crashes*, it should create a folder called `EquilinoxErrorLogs` in the mod directory, with an `ERROR_.txt` file. Both of these files can help me diagnose an issue. I could also benefit from seeing the save file for the world, which you can find in the `Equilinox_AP_Saves` folder. Note, this folder gets created in the main game directory, not in the mod's EquilinoxAP file. This means you can update the mod without losing existing save files (however, you should pay attention to any compatibility warnings on new releases). If your issue pertains to save file loading, then I will definitely want to see this file. Inside this folder should be your save files. Note that the game can not read these files without the mod running, so you shouldn't have to worry about them if you decide to play vanilla. > [!WARNING] > Connection information is saved in your save file. Without the game, the .dat file alone is not enough to view it (ie, you can't just open the file in Notepad). But if someone else loads your save file in game, it will try to connect automatically. If you don't feel comfortable sharing these files in the public server, you are welcome to DM them to me on Discord instead (username `aaces17`).

notes.text:
## Changelog

### General Changes/Additions
- Replaced "Evolve Camel" goal with "Evolve Species" goal: 
  - Choose a set of species and a count `n` (defaults to all selected species), where you need to evolve `n` of the species in the set to send the goal
- Add "Progressive DP/Min Bonus" item:
  - Yaml option to add 0 - 40 (default 10) of these to the item pool. Having received `n` of these items, you will have a constant bonus of `+15(n^2+n) dp/min`
- Notable logic changes:
  - Logically require dp generation (either via the new "Progressive DP/Min Bonus" item or via animals) for most purchases and evolutions
  - More tasks and evolutions logically require species satisfaction
    - (While I tested many of these changes, please report any checks that appear in logic too early in case I missed some)
- Add item groups for unlock permits: `Tier 1 Plant Permits`, `Tier 1 Animal Permits`, `Stone Permits`, and `Large Rock Permits`. 
- Fix .apworld manifest?


### Minor Client Changes
- Display connection status, received dp items, and goal progress in the AP Toolbar menu
- Make fast-forward (the double arrow button on the bottom bar) a toggle instead of a press-and-hold
- Send in-game notification when trying to connect
- Mouseover of locked tier 1 shop items now displays "Find in the multiworld: ______ Permit" instead of "Unlocked by task: _______"


## Updating the Mod

View the [Setup Guide](https://github.com/AAces17/EquilinoxAPClient#setup-instructions) on the Github repository.

This updated client should be compatible with worlds generated on any v0.1.x. However, updating the client mid-run is not necessary unless you really want the new QOL features.
